summary: A short, non-interactive status label like Draft, Published or Failed. The words carry the meaning; the tone reinforces it. With appearance count, the count tag next to a label.
whenToUse: The status of one item in a table row, a list or a card header.
subtle (default) in lists and tables where many badges sit together; solid for the single status that must win a glance (Breaking, Build failed).
Tone by meaning: success done or healthy, warning needs attention, danger failed or blocked, info new or changed, neutral no judgement.

appearance count for a number next to its label (Explorations 2, Colors 4): ink figures in tabular numbers on a neutral fill, no border, and the stronger tone inside the current nav item, the selected tab or the checked segment. It is the same count tag Tabs, SegmentedControl and SidebarNav render from their count prop, so use those props there.

Plain-script pages that build rows as HTML strings use badgeHtml() from @bridge-ds/react/dom: the same markup, tones and sizes, without React. Never a homemade pill: the design system audit counts those as look-alikes.
whenNotToUse: Anything clickable or removable: use Tag.
A sentence or an explanation: use an inline Alert.
Counts on icons: use the number in text next to the label.

dos.title: The text says the status, the tone backs it up
dos.text: Someone who cannot tell green from red still reads Published and Failed.

dos.title: Counts in the count tag
dos.text: A number next to a label uses appearance count: dark figures that read at a glance, on a fill that stays a tag on the page and on the side nav ground.

dos.title: Subtle in rows, solid for the exception
dos.text: A table full of solid badges shouts. Keep solid for the one thing that must stand out.

donts.title: Color as the only signal
donts.text: A dot without words fails WCAG 1.4.1 and means nothing to a screen reader.

donts.title: A count as a neutral status
donts.text: Muted figures in a bordered status pill read as disabled. Counts take appearance count, not tone neutral.

donts.title: A tone that contradicts the words
donts.text: Danger for New borrows urgency the user did not ask for.

accessibility: Static text read in reading order. No role, not focusable.
Subtle tones use feedback text on feedback bg (4.5:1); solid tones use text.on-solid on feedback solid (4.5:1). Checked by the token build in every brand and theme.

The count tag puts text.default on the emphasis neutral (7:1 or more in every brand and theme) and text.inverse on surface.inverse in the current or selected item (15:1). Give it an accessible name when the number alone is unclear ("2 waiting on you").
The dot and icon are decorative; the text carries the status.
If a status changes while the user watches (Running to Failed), announce it with a live region; the badge itself is silent.
contentGuidelines: One or two words, sentence case: "Needs review", not "NEEDS REVIEW".
Past participles for finished states (Published, Merged), present for ongoing (Running).

anatomy.count: Count appearance: ink tabular figures on a neutral fill
